title: Irfan Pathan Exposes Fake Story About Babar Azam Interview Snub
excerpt: The former India all-rounder says Pakistani media photoshopped his face into a fabricated video claiming Babar Azam refused him an interview, and the clip racked up over a million views.
body:
• Irfan Pathan has revealed that Pakistani media fabricated a story claiming Babar Azam refused to give him an interview during the 2023 ODI World Cup, saying they photoshopped his face into the video.
  • The fake clip, first aired by a Pakistani journalist on Aaj TV, went viral and accumulated over a million views across social media platforms.
  • Former India spinner Harbhajan Singh publicly defended Pathan, pointing out he was nowhere in the video, and Pathan responded that the trolls "want reach by lying."
  • Pathan says he chooses not to engage with every provocation, adding "you can't live life if you keep responding" to fabricated content.

Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has broken his silence on a fabricated story that went viral across social media, revealing that Pakistani media outlets photoshopped his face into a video and falsely claimed Pakistan captain Babar Azam had refused to give him an interview.

"They photoshopped my face," Pathan said, describing how the fake narrative was constructed and amplified. The fabricated story, he revealed, accumulated over a million views across platforms, turning a complete fiction into what many fans accepted as fact.

How the Fake Story Originated

The fabrication traces back to the 2023 ODI World Cup in India. Pakistani journalist Naseem Rajput claimed on the Aaj TV show 'Kuch Cricket Ho Jaye' that Babar Azam had twice refused Pathan's request for an interview — first through the channel's production team, then when Pathan allegedly approached Babar directly. Rajput claimed Babar told Pathan he "doesn't talk to those who speak against Pakistan."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=-beAhJ4p8uE

CricTracker investigated the claim at the time and found it to be "absolutely baseless," reporting that no such incident ever took place. Despite the debunking, the story spread rapidly across social media without verification.

The fabrication resurfaced in 2024, when a fan account dedicated to Babar Azam posted a video on X showing the Pakistan captain walking past a reporter on the boundary. The account falsely captioned it: "When @IrfanPathan begs to Babar Azam for Interview and he refused." Pathan was not in the video at all.

Harbhajan Singh Fires Back

Former India spinner Harbhajan Singh was among the first to call out the deception. He responded on X, questioning the poster's credibility and pointing out the obvious: Pathan was nowhere to be seen in the clip.

"Where is Irfan Pathan in this video? You people never had the decency to speak. Now have you stopped seeing with your eyes as well?"

— Harbhajan Singh, on X

Pathan himself weighed in, urging Harbhajan to ignore the provocation. "Inko jhoot bolke REACH chahiye. Ignore maaro Paaji," he wrote — translated as "They want reach by lying. Ignore them, brother."

Pathan's Broader Message

Now speaking in greater detail about the episode, Pathan has addressed the broader problem of fabricated content in cricket media. He said the fake story was deliberately designed to inflame India-Pakistan tensions and drive engagement, and that such content exploits the intensity of the rivalry for clicks and views.

"You can't live life if you keep responding" to every piece of misinformation, Pathan said, explaining why he had largely chosen to let the matter pass rather than engage with each new iteration of the false narrative.

The episode highlights a recurring pattern in India-Pakistan cricket dynamics, where fabricated content and manipulated media regularly circulate during and after major tournaments. During the Pahalgam crisis in 2025, doctored sketches altered to resemble Babar Azam circulated widely before being debunked through digital forensic analysis.

Context: The Rivalry Off the Pitch

Pathan, a former T20 World Cup winner who has transitioned into broadcasting and commentary, has been a regular target of trolling from Pakistani fans, particularly after India's victories over Pakistan in the 2023 ODI World Cup, the 2024 T20 World Cup, and the 2026 T20 World Cup in Colombo. He has previously drawn attention for his sharp commentary on Babar Azam's form, including his call to "stop comparing Babar Azam with Virat Kohli" after Azam's five-run knock in the 2026 India-Pakistan clash.

For the Indian diaspora, the story resonates as a case study in how misinformation can target public figures and weaponize cricket's cultural significance in South Asian communities. Pathan's decision to speak openly about the fabrication serves as a reminder that even widely viewed content can be entirely manufactured.
